summary: Ubay bin Ka'b said that after the Prophet passed away, the Companions who had been united while with him began looking in different directions.
notes: The Prophet is not named in the text (OCR gap at 'When with,'); marked mentioned from the heading. The second version is introduced by 'Another narration' from the same narrator.

summary: Anas bin Maalik said Madinah turned dark on the day the Prophet passed away, and recalled that the day he entered Madinah was the brightest day and the day of his death the darkest.
notes: Two separate Anas reports are joined: the darkness after the death, and the comparison of the Hijrah day with the day of death. An OCR footnote fragment (Ibn Abi Dunya, Kanzul Ummaal) sits in the middle and was ignored.

summary: Anas reports that Abu Talha, seeing the consultative council appointed by Umar competing to be the next caliph, said he feared more that they would pass the office on to another, and that Umar's death had left every Muslim home at a loss.
notes: The quotation has no closing quote mark or full stop and stops after 'death of Umar'; it may be cut at a page break.

summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas said that when the Mushrikeen asked the Prophet to drive away the poor Sahabah, among them Bilaal and Ibn Mas'ood, Allaah revealed the verse forbidding him to do so.
notes: The Mushrikeen and the unnamed Banu Hudhayl Sahabi and the two unnamed Sahabah are left out.

summary: Ibn Mas'ood reports that when a group of the Quraysh asked the Prophet to drive away poor Muslims such as Suhayb, Bilaal, Khabbaab and Ammaar, Allaah revealed Surah An'aam verses 51 and 52.
notes: The Quraysh speakers are unnamed and left out.

summary: Anas and Aa'isha report that while the Prophet was inviting Ubay bin Khalaf to Islaam, the blind Ibn Umm Maktoom came to him, and that Surah Abasa was revealed; afterwards the Prophet always honoured Ibn Umm Maktoom.
notes: Anas and Aa'isha give separate reports of the same incident, joined without a break. Ubay bin Khalaf is not in the approved list (Umayyah bin Khalaf is a different person). OCR debris 'Discussing the verse j' ignored.

summary: Khabbaab bin Arat relates that Aqra and Uyayna asked the Prophet to send away the poor Sahabah before the delegations saw them, and that Allaah revealed verses commanding him to stay with them, after which the Companions sat close to him.
notes: Jibra'eel (the angel) is left out. Aqra and Uyayna are named as Tameemi and Fazaari in the text and linked to the Companion entries.

summary: Salmaan reports that Uyayna and Aqra asked the Prophet to move the poor Muslims in woollen cloaks away from him so they could sit and learn with him, and that Allaah revealed Surah Kahf verses 27 and 28 forbidding him to obey such people.
notes: Cut off mid-sentence after 'amongst you shall I'.

summary: Abu Salma reports that Qais bin Mataatiyyah belittled Salmaan, Suhayb and Bilaal, and that Mu'aadh seized him and brought him to the Prophet, who told the people that all are of one Rabb, one father and one Deen, and that Arabic makes no one superior, and said to leave the man to the Fire.
notes: Qais bin Mataatiyyah is not in the approved list; the text calls him a Munaafiq and says he was killed, so sahabi is no. The text ends mid-sentence ('killed in this'). An OCR footnote (Abu Nu'aym) is in the middle and was ignored. Abu Salma's sahabi status is unsure per the approved list.

summary: Buraydah reports that a man asked whether he had repaid his mother by carrying her on his neck across scorching sands, and the Prophet said it may have repaid only a single labour pain.
notes: 'Buraydah' is a bare name; linked to buraydah-bin-husayb. The approved list also has buraydah-bin-khusayb, which is probably the same man. The man who asked is unnamed.

summary: Aa'isha reports that when a man came with his elderly father, the Prophet told him never to walk or sit before his father, never to call him by name, and never to make him the target of abuse.
notes: The man and his father are unnamed.

summary: Abu Ghassaan Dhabi says that Abu Hurayrah met him walking with his father and advised him to walk behind or beside his father, not to let anyone come between them, not to walk on an unrailed roof, and not to eat meat his father was eyeing.
notes: Abu Ghassaan Dhabi is not in the approved list and his status as a Companion is unclear. The father is unnamed.

summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that when a man asked to join Jihaad, the Prophet asked whether his parents were alive and told him that his Jihaad was to be with them.
notes: The man is unnamed.

summary: Three reports say that men who wished to migrate or wage Jihaad were told to return to their parents and be good to them, and a man from Yemen was told he could fight only with his parents' permission.
notes: Three separate reports: an unnamed man who pledged to migrate, a second man who had left his weeping parents, and Abu Sa'eed's account of a man from Yemen. The men are unnamed.

summary: Anas reports that a man who wanted to march in Jihaad but lacked the means was told that serving his mother would bring him the reward of Hajj, Umrah and Jihaad.
notes: The man is unnamed.

summary: Abu Umaamah reports that when the Prophet called the Muslims to march on Khaybar, Abu Hurayrah stayed behind to care for his mother, and the Prophet told him that being with his parents and fulfilling their rights is also in the path of Allaah.
notes: The text itself says 'The narration still continues further', so this item stops at that point. Abu Hurayrah's mother is unnamed.

summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that a woman brought her son, who wanted to join Jihaad, to the Prophet at Siqaayah, and the Prophet told him to stay with his mother until she permitted him or died, as that would earn him greater reward.
notes: The woman and her son are unnamed.

summary: A narration states that a man wanting to fight in Jihaad, whose mother was against it, was told by the Prophet to stay close to her, as his reward with her would equal the reward of Jihaad.
notes: No narrator is named ('Another narration states'). The text ends on a comma with no closing quotation mark and may be cut off. The man and his mother are unnamed.

summary: Talha bin Mu'aawiya Sulami reports that he asked the Prophet's permission to wage Jihaad, and was told to stay at his mother's feet because Jannah lies there.
notes: Talha bin Mu'aawiya Sulami is not in the approved list (Talha bin Ubaydillaah and Talha bin Amr are different people).

summary: Jaahimah reports that when he came to the Prophet for advice about Jihaad, he was asked whether his parents were alive, and was told to stay with them because Jannah lies beneath their feet.
notes: Jaahimah is not in the approved list.

summary: Jaahimah recounts asking the Prophet about Jihaad, being told to stay with his mother because Jannah lies beneath her feet, and receiving the same answer on repeated asking.
notes: Same Companion as n01660 (name only); Jaahimah is not in the approved list.

summary: Nu'aym reports that Abdullaah bin Umar, sitting beneath a tree between Makkah and Madinah, recalled seeing a young man ask the Prophet to join Jihaad and being told to go back and be good to his parents.
notes: Nu'aym is described as the freed slave of Umm Salamah. He is not linked to nuaym-bin-abdillaah because the identity is not confirmed. The young man is unnamed.

summary: Hasan narrates that when Umar proposed for Ummu Kulthoom, Ali said she was too young; after Umar cited his kinship with the Prophet and Ali's sons objected, Ali told them to get the proposer married.
notes: The narrator 'Hasan' is not Hasan bin Ali, who appears in the story; probably Hasan al-Basri, so left unlinked for review. Ummu Kulthoom is linked to ummu-kulthoom, presumed to be the daughter of Ali.

summary: Ibn Seereen reports that when a date palm's sap was prized at a thousand dirhams, Usaama bored into a palm and gave the sap to his mother because she had asked for it.
notes: The first name is lost to OCR ('Hadhrat (RA) bin Seereen'). The approved list has both usaama and usaama-bin-zaid; the bare name was linked to usaama and should be checked. Usaama's mother is unnamed.

summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that the Prophet came down from the pulpit to lift Husayn after the child tripped on his cloth during the sermon, saying that children are a trial.
Abu Sa'eed and Zubayr report that Hasan climbed onto the Prophet's back while he was in sajdah, and the Prophet did not rise or move him until the boy chose to get down.
notes: Two separate reports with different narrators: Abu Sa'eed, then Zubayr. 'Abu Sa'eed' is a bare name and is linked to abu-saeed-khudri; abu-saeed-bin-fudaala is also in the approved list.

summary: Bahiy reports that Ibn Zubayr described Hasan as the grandson most like the Prophet and most beloved to him, who would climb onto his back during salaah and be left there until he got down.
notes: Bahiy is not in the approved list.

summary: Ibn Mas'ood and Anas report that Hasan and Husayn would climb onto the Prophet's back during sajdah, and that he prolonged the sajdah, saying he did not like to rise quickly while his grandsons were on him.
notes: Two separate reports with different narrators: Ibn Mas'ood, then Anas. The Companions who tried to stop the boys are unnamed.

summary: Abu Qataadah reports that the Prophet came out with his granddaughter Umaamah on his shoulders and prayed, putting her down for ruku and lifting her again after sajdah.
notes: 'Abu Qataadah' is a bare name and is linked to abu-qataadah; the approved list also has abu-qataada and Abu Qataadah Haarith bin Rib'ee. Umaamah bint Abil Aas is not in the approved list.

summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet came out carrying Hasan on one shoulder and Husayn on the other, kissing each in turn, and said that whoever loves them loves him and whoever hates them hates him.
notes: The person who asked the question is unnamed.

summary: Mu'aawiya reports that he saw the Prophet suck Hasan's tongue and said that a tongue or lips the Prophet had sucked could never suffer punishment.
notes: The bare name 'Mu'aawiya' could be Mu'aawiya bin Abi Sufyaan or another holder of the name, so it is left unlinked for review.

summary: Saa'ib bin Yazeed reports that when the Prophet kissed Hasan, Aqra said he had ten children and had never kissed one of them, and the Prophet replied that Allaah does not show mercy to those who do not show mercy to people.
Aswad bin Khalaf reports that the Prophet kissed Hasan and said that a child makes a man miserly, foolish and cowardly, because he fears for the child's welfare.
notes: Aswad bin Khalaf is not in the approved list (Aswad bin Abdil Muttalib is a different person).

summary: Anas reports that the Prophet was the most compassionate towards his family and visited his son Ibraheem, who was nursed at a blacksmith's home, kissing and smelling the child.
notes: Ibraheem is taken to be the Prophet's son, matching the approved entry ibraheem (no). Please confirm that entry is the son and not the Prophet Ibraheem. The blacksmith's wife is unnamed.

summary: Anas reports that after Aa'isha told the Prophet how a mother split her last date between her two daughters, he said she would surely enter Jannah for that deed.
notes: The mother is unnamed.

summary: Hasan bin Ali reports that the Prophet gave a mother's two sons one date each and that she split her own date between them, and he said Allaah would show her mercy; Abu Hurayrah then reports the Prophet asking a father whether he is merciful to his child.
notes: Three parts: Hasan's date report, Abu Hurayrah's report of the father and child, and a fused fragment about the Prophet forbidding anyone who has harmed his neighbour from joining a battle, with no narrator named. The OCR breaks mid-sentence in the Abu Hurayrah part ('towards you than you are towards your leaving for a battle'). The mother and sons are unnamed.

summary: Miqdaad reports that the Prophet asked the Sahabah about adultery and theft, and said that both are more serious when committed against one's neighbour than against others.
notes: The text says Miqdaad bin Aswad; the approved entry is Miqdaad bin Amr, who is also called bin al-Aswad, so this looks like the same Companion. Please check.

summary: Mutarrif reports Abu Dharr's hadith that Allaah loves three kinds of people, beginning with one who fights with steadfastness in the path of Allaah; the passage then gives Aa'isha's account of the Prophet's teaching to treat people according to their status.
notes: Three parts: Mutarrif's report of Abu Dharr's hadith, Aa'isha's account of the rich guest and the beggar, and a back-reference to Ali giving clothes and gold to a man. OCR fused a Qur'anic verse into the Aa'isha part, mid-line. Mutarrif is not in the approved list and may be a Tabi'i although the text says RA; check.

summary: Aghar reports that Abu Bakr greeted everyone he saw from afar with salaam before they could greet him, and Zuhrah bin Khameesa reports Abu Bakr saying people had outdone them in returning greetings.
notes: Two separate reports: Aghar's, then Zuhrah bin Khameesa's (not in the approved list). The Ansaari is unnamed. Aghar is linked to the approved entry aghar, which is marked unsure.

summary: Umar reports riding behind Abu Bakr, who greeted every group they passed, and that the replies were fuller than the greeting, prompting Abu Bakr to remark that people had surpassed them greatly that day.
